text_blocks.snippet: A pulmonologist uses several tests to diagnose asthma, with spirometry being the most common initial test. This test measures how much air you can exhale and how quickly, revealing if airways are narrowed, a key sign of asthma. Other tests include bronchoprovocation testing, which may involve inhaling methacholine, a substance that can trigger airway narrowing, or exercise, to assess airway responsiveness. Additionally, FeNO testing, which measures nitric oxide in exhaled breath, can indicate lung inflammation characteristic of asthma. Blood tests may also be used to check for eosinophils and IgE antibodies, which can be elevated in some asthma cases.
